name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,909

clue.text: Mummy cases good here?

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so MUM encloses the next word

blocks.note: MUM = mummy, opened after its first letter
use = good, as in 'is it any use?'

explanation.surface: A visitor wonders whether a place displays fine Egyptian sarcophagi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy cases' reads as sarcophagi, and read straight the whole clue still describes the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: museums are where Egyptian mummy cases are put on show, so the whole clue describes the place.

clue.text: Baby in India punches like an adult

indicators.note: to punch is to drive into something, so IN I goes inside MATURE

blocks.note: I = India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An infant in India throws punches like a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' is an adjective here, as in a baby carrot, not an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: a baby version of something is a small-scale one, as in baby grand, and that is a miniature.

clue.text: Penny feeds children in hurry

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so P goes inside SEED

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny rushes to get the children fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; it is just the P of British money.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain verb synonym: to hurry somewhere is to speed there, go fast.

clue.text: Later note butcher with uniform on improve at work

indicators.note: in a down answer, something put on the rest sits above it, so U goes first

blocks.note: U = uniform in the NATO alphabet
PS = postscript, a note added later

explanation.surface: A memo tells a butcher to put on his uniform and get better at his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' is a verb, not the shopkeeper it poses as, and 'with' just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern jargon: to upskill is to gain new abilities for your job, improving at work.

clue.text: Make spouse on end of chorus line pirouette

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, S of chorus
in an across answer, WIVE put on S follows it

blocks.note: to wive is to take a wife, to make someone your spouse

explanation.surface: A chorus-line dancer marries and the line turns a pirouette.
explanation.walkthrough: WIVE is an old verb for marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: a pirouette is a spin on one spot, and to swivel is to turn round on a fixed point.

clue.text: Rearing stunt that's fun on a little bull

indicators.note: in a down answer, something on another sits above it, so WHEE comes first

blocks.note: bull = nonsense, and a lie is a small piece of it

explanation.surface: A rodeo rider enjoys a stunt on a young bull that rears up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' looks like the animal, which fits 'rearing'; it is bull meaning nonsense or untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: in a wheelie a cyclist lifts the front wheel so the bike rears up like a horse.

clue.text: Express train leaves Berlin regularly

indicators.note: to train something is to shape it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
at regular intervals, taking every other letter of Berlin

blocks.note: B, R, I: first, third and fifth letters of Berlin

explanation.surface: An express train pulls out of Berlin on a regular timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express train' reads as one thing; it splits into the definition and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to express a thought is to put it into words, which is to verbalise it.

clue.text: Trousers reflecting the King's first pair?

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things back to front
only the first two letters are turned round

blocks.note: Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: A question about the jeans Elvis wore first.
explanation.walkthrough: Only EL flips; VIS stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Levi's are a brand of denim jeans, one kind of trousers.

clue.text: Chain attached to pet defended by church people

indicators.note: defenders stand around what they protect, so CE surrounds ONCAT

explanation.surface: Churchgoers protect a pet that is kept on a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain attached to pet' reads as a lead; 'attached to' is really ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a concatenation is a series of things linked end to end, as the links of a chain are.

clue.text: Teenage stress?

blocks.note: surface: adolescent; setter's reading: aged under a score, a score being twenty
surface: anxiety; setter's reading: the verb, to emphasise

explanation.surface: A pop-psychology heading about adolescent anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer says 'under twenty', which is teenage; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to stress a point is to emphasise it, as a line drawn beneath words does.

clue.text: Party not smiling when leader's ousted

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, and ousting it throws it out

blocks.note: grave = solemn, not smiling; its G then goes

explanation.surface: A political party looks glum after its leader is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is politics; the party is a dance event.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a rave is a big all-night dance party.

clue.text: Irish cops pull over driver of Waymo taxi, say

indicators.note: turned over, like a page, so DRAG runs backwards

blocks.note: Waymo taxis are driverless, steered by artificial intelligence

explanation.surface: Irish police stop a self-driving taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull over' looks like one phrasal verb, but it is PULL turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional word: the Garda Síochána is the police of the Republic of Ireland, and gardaí is the plural for its officers.

clue.text: Totally twisted wood fences come down

indicators.note: twisted round, so ALL faces the other way
a fence surrounds a field, so COPSE surrounds the reversed word

blocks.note: a copse is a small wood

explanation.surface: Wooden fences, badly warped, fall over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood fences' reads as timber fencing; wood is COPSE and 'fences' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: when a building comes down it falls in on itself, it collapses.

clue.text: Explorer showing bravery faced with missionary's head in shack

indicators.note: a face is at the front, so M stands before BOLD
the head of a word is its first letter
in means inside, so M BOLD is placed within the shack, HUT

explanation.surface: A brave explorer meets a missionary in a jungle hut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'Explorer' and 'missionary' into one colonial scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Alexander von Humboldt was a German naturalist who explored South America around 1800.

clue.text: One showing technique amid a lot of drinking?

definitions.text: One showing technique amid a lot of drinking?

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so ART sits inside BENDER

blocks.note: a bender is a drinking spree

explanation.surface: Someone shows off skill in a noisy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: a bartender shows off mixing technique while surrounded by people drinking heavily.

clue.text: Cryptic magazine missing separate parts of Azed puzzle

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure, hidden in meaning, so the letters are disguised by rearranging
lacking, so A and Z are taken out of MAGAZINE

blocks.note: A and Z, separate letters of AZED, removed

explanation.surface: A cryptic crossword magazine lacks parts of an Azed puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about crosswords; Azed is the Observer's crossword setter, and only his A and Z are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an enigma is a mystery or riddle, a puzzle.

clue.text: Wrongly award MBEs to women claiming income support

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so MBES TO W takes IS inside

blocks.note: IS = Income Support, a UK benefit

explanation.surface: Honours go wrongly to women who are on state benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: An MBE is a British honour. The clue words are almost the answer's letters as printed: only IS is slipped in after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed from mis- (wrongly) and bestow (award), so the definition is the word taken apart.

clue.text: Light French cheese sounded rubbish

indicators.note: sounded means spoken aloud, so the words count for their sound

blocks.note: light = day, and brie is a French cheese

explanation.surface: A mild French cheese proved to be garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like it describes the cheese; it is DAY, daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: debris is scattered broken remains, rubbish.

clue.text: Writer given reduced portion initially in strop

indicators.note: cut down, so SHARE loses its last letter
at the start, so the shortened portion goes first

explanation.surface: A writer in a sulk because his share was cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strop' looks like the British word for a sulk; here it is the verb for sharpening a razor on a leather strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Specialised verb: a strop is a leather strap, and to strop a razor is to sharpen it on one.

clue.text: In part, Palestine area's title?

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A question about what the region around Palestine is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden answer is also what the surface asks for, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: the Near East is a name for the region that includes Palestine, and part of it is what the clue asks for.

clue.text: Examination someone's suspiciously late for?

blocks.note: surface: a school exam; setter's reading: a medical examination of a body
surface: a candidate turns up oddly late; setter's reading: someone has died, late meaning dead, in suspicious circumstances

explanation.surface: An exam that a candidate arrives at oddly late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: an autopsy is the examination held when someone has died in suspicious circumstances.

clue.text: Radioactive part of reactor stable according to Spooner's calculation

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: the core of a reactor holds the fuel; it takes the F of FAST
fast = firmly fixed, stable; it takes the C of CORE

explanation.surface: A nuclear engineer's calculation that the reactor core is stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' looks like a noun for horses; it means steady, FAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a forecast is a reckoning of what will happen, a calculation of the future.

clue.text: Patent Tesla is subject to?

indicators.note: to be subject to something is to be under it, so in a down answer OVER sits above T

blocks.note: what T is subject to is over it
T = tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A question about which patents the car maker Tesla holds.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car company; it is the physics unit T. 'Patent' is the adjective, meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: patent means plain for all to see, and overt means done openly.

clue.text: Husband coming out of dense bushes gets fixed penalty notice, say

indicators.note: the husband emerges from the bushes, so H leaves THICKET

blocks.note: a thicket is a dense growth of bushes

explanation.surface: A man emerging from the undergrowth is handed a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A fixed penalty notice is a British on-the-spot fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'say': a parking or speeding ticket is a fixed penalty notice.

clue.text: Pink bit of candy in your mouth

indicators.note: a small bit, just the first letter of candy

explanation.surface: A piece of pink sweet sits in your mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like the candy's colour; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour name: coral, after the sea creature's skeleton, is a pinkish-orange shade.

clue.text: Crook close to shepherd on mountain

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, the D of shepherd
in an across answer, D put on BEN comes after it

blocks.note: ben = Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A shepherd's crook, held by him up on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' suggests a criminal or a shepherd's staff; it means a bend, as in the crook of the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: the crook of your arm or a crook in a road is a curve, a bend.

clue.text: Good times for dodgy priest ending in ignominy

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound, not in proper shape, so PRIEST is rearranged
the ending of a word is its last letter, Y of ignominy

explanation.surface: A corrupt priest enjoys good times before ending in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface tells a morality tale; 'for' is PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: prosperity is a period of wealth and success, good times.

clue.text: Chair perplexed by speaker

indicators.note: as said by a speaker, so the word counts for how it is pronounced

explanation.surface: The chairman is baffled by what the speaker says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the Commons Speaker's chair; here it only signals a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a throne is a monarch's ceremonial chair.

clue.text: Secondary concussion that might make you wobbly

definitions.text: Secondary concussion that might make you wobbly

blocks.note: by- = secondary, as in byroad or by-product
a concussion is a violent blow or shock

explanation.surface: A second knock to the head leaves you unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: A by-blow also means an illegitimate child, which is not the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: a by-blow is a side blow, a secondary knock of the kind that leaves you wobbly.
